newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian health workers talk, no strike deal seen.
newsitem.headline: Colombian health workers talk, no strike deal seen.

text.p: Labour leaders said on Monday that there was a positive atmosphere in talks aimed at solving a week-old strike by Colombian doctors, nurses and health workers but no immediate deal was in sight.

An estimated 120,000 workers in the state-run health sector called the strike to protest the government's failure to meet a wage deal reached at the end of a weeklong stoppage by all state employees in February.
"There's nothing firm yet but we've started talks and there's a will for dialogue," said Yesid Camacho, head of the national Hospital Workers Union (ANTHOC).
Talks began last weekend following the return of Health Minister Maria Teresa Forero de Saade, who had been abroad.
"The health workers expressed their desire to talk and if the strike is lifted then we can take a proposal to Congress to find more funds," she told reporters.

Under the February deal, the government agreed to give all public-sector workers a pay hike worth about 20 percent, with an additional payment to health workers to bring their wages into line with other professions.
The government has so far said, however, that it must present a bill to Congress to try and win an additional budget allocation to meet the pledge on salaries.
Salvador Varela, a regional head of the medical union ASMEDAS, said the strike would not be lifted until the government guaranteed extra funds were available to meet workers' demands.
"A formula exists to end this strike but we must look for the mechanism to achieve this aim. The government must this budget increase through Congress," he said.
The stoppage has brought routine surgery and appointments to a halt in state-run hospitals and medical centres across the country although emergency services are unaffected.
